feature: joint-task activation notifications and accessible dialog names
rules: Activating a joint task through the interface creates one event per other authorized participant and superior, filtered by active profile, company, and canWork access.
The task participant can open the notification from the header bell and reach the exact task.
Opening the notice marks only that recipient's event as read, and the state survives reload without generating duplicate events.
Shared dialogs expose their visible heading through aria-labelledby so assistive technology receives the dialog name.

assertions: The 60/40 joint allocation persists from the setup UI.
Exactly the other authorized participants and superior receive one activation notice.
The invited participant sees the notice, opens the task, and its read status persists after reload.
Two member clocks remain independent; completion and sequential closures preserve personal reports and CSV privacy.
The existing desktop and mobile laboratory workflows, drag-and-drop, and correction flows pass.

verification.preCommit: passed: scripts/validate-change.mjs; 96/96 tests in 14 files, TypeScript and cached diff check

buildNotes: Vite succeeds with the existing informational main JavaScript chunk warning at approximately 593 kB, above 500 kB.
Rollup removes two upstream Zod purity comments; this does not prevent the build.
limitations: Notifications remain in browser-local paris-state-lab and do not synchronize between devices.
No email, account, operational API, D1, or Supabase was used.
Server-side event delivery and authorization need a separate architecture review before implementation.
